narrative:
The model determined that you have an 84% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this predicted risk is so high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Your rejection was driven first and foremost by your class ranking at the end of your third year. You placed in the bottom decile of your class, far below the average student who was accepted. This single factor was the strongest reason the model expected you to struggle on the bar. Your first-year ranking reinforced the same message: you also finished in the bottom decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. These two academic standing measures together created a powerful signal that you would likely have difficulty passing the bar.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 actually worked slightly in your favor. It sits a bit above the average of students who were admitted, so the model saw this as a modest positive. Unfortunately, it was not nearly enough to offset the much stronger negative influence of your class rankings.

The next step is to focus on improving your academic performance and building stronger evidence that you can succeed on the bar. Consider retaking key courses, seeking academic support, or gaining additional legal experience that demonstrates your ability before reapplying. This clearer picture of your record will help future applications. (218 words)
